justification: Payments (Stripe Checkout redirect construction) — Critical per CLAUDE.md's own QA tier table. The defect: pre-da-history/route.ts built its Stripe success_url/cancel_url from the raw, attacker-controlled request Origin header instead of the server-side NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL env var every sibling checkout route already uses. An attacker hosting their own page could POST to this route and have Stripe's post-payment redirect point at their own domain -- a customer completing a real $49 payment would be sent to the attacker's site instead of PlotDetect's. Also fixed the same dead-apex fallback default (plotdetect.com.au -> verify.plotdetect.com.au) that #1009/786fb4a7 already fixed on every other route, since this file predates that fix and still carried it on main.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: success_url or cancel_url is built from the request Origin header (or any other client-supplied value) rather than exclusively from process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL, or the fallback default reverts to the dead bare apex.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Forced red by reverting only route.ts (git stash) with the test file present: 3 of 9 tests failed -- 'ignores an attacker-controlled Origin header entirely' failed because success_url contained a URL built from https://plotdetect.com.au (the OLD code path) rather than rejecting the attacker Origin outright, and the two fallback tests failed on the dead-apex string, matching exactly what the fix closes. Restored: 9/9 green. Full jest suite: 95 suites / 1282 tests green. tsc clean.

pre_impl.existing_data: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL is the single source of truth for this value across all 13 sibling stripe checkout routes and the webhook (grepped: none of them read req.headers.get('origin') at all). pre-da-history/route.ts was the sole outlier -- confirmed by grepping the full frontend-nextjs/app/api tree for headers.get('origin'): only this file and app/api/ai/chat-honeypot/route.ts matched, and chat-honeypot only logs the value for bot-detection telemetry, never uses it to build a URL.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Assumed initially (from Sol's first-round finding) that this pattern was duplicated 'across all similarly changed checkout routes' -- verified false by reading each of the other 13 files directly. The blast radius is exactly one file, not the whole payment surface.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Existing rows (past Stripe sessions already created with the old, vulnerable origin) are unaffected -- Stripe checkout sessions and their redirect URLs are generated once at session-creation time and are not retroactively alterable by this code change. This only changes what a NEW checkout session gets as its success/cancel URL.
pre_impl.external_source_error: N/A for this change -- no external call changes shape. getStripe() and stripe.checkout.sessions.create() are unchanged calls; only the string fed into success_url/cancel_url changes, and Stripe itself returns the same session object either way.
pre_impl.frontend_type: No. The response shape ({ checkout_url }) is unchanged; only the value's content (which domain the redirect points at) differs, and no frontend type reads that content directly.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: None new, and the fix closes an existing silent one. Before the fix, a customer arriving via an attacker's link would complete a real payment and be redirected to the attacker's site post-payment with no visible error at all -- the silent failure this fix closes. After the fix, every customer is redirected to plotdetect's own verify subdomain regardless of what page or link they arrived from; if NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL is ever unset, the fallback is now the live app domain, not a 404.

functions.name: POST
functions.input: NextRequest with JSON body { report_id, email, firm_name? } and arbitrary request headers, including an attacker-settable Origin
functions.output: NextResponse — 200 with { checkout_url }, or 400/500 with { error }
functions.if_none: Origin header absent or attacker-controlled: no longer read at all; origin is now derived exclusively from process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL, falling back to the correct https://verify.plotdetect.com.au default if that env var is unset

values.nullable: NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL may be unset in some environments (e.g. a misconfigured preview deploy)
values.guard_at: the ?? fallback default on the same line
values.if_missing: falls back to https://verify.plotdetect.com.au — the live, correct app domain — never a dead or attacker-supplied value

break_it.scenario: An attacker hosts a page at https://attacker.example that POSTs to this route with a customer's browser, using a real report_id and email the attacker phished or guessed.
break_it.what_happens: Before the fix: the browser's Origin header (https://attacker.example, truthfully sent — a browser cannot lie about its own origin) becomes the base of success_url/cancel_url. The customer pays PlotDetect $49 via a real Stripe session, then Stripe redirects them to https://attacker.example/reports/pre-da-history?payment=success&report_id=... after payment, where the attacker controls the page the customer lands on immediately post-payment.
break_it.how: origin is now read exclusively from the server-side NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL env var; the request object's headers are never consulted for this value.
break_it.repro: checkout-pre-da-history.test.ts: 'ignores an attacker-controlled Origin header entirely' — forced red on the pre-fix code, confirmed green after

break_it.scenario: No Origin header is sent at all (a server-to-server call, curl, or a browser configuration that omits it).
break_it.what_happens: Before the fix: fell back to the dead bare apex (https://plotdetect.com.au), which 404s on every app route per 786fb4a7's own live-curl evidence. Same defect class as the 14-file fix already merged elsewhere, just never applied to this file.
break_it.how: The fallback default is now https://verify.plotdetect.com.au, the live app domain, matching every sibling checkout route.
break_it.repro: checkout-pre-da-history.test.ts: 'uses NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL when no Origin header is present at all'

break_it.scenario: NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL is unset in a given deploy environment (e.g. a misconfigured preview branch).
break_it.what_happens: success_url/cancel_url would silently point at whatever the fallback string is.
break_it.how: Fallback is hardcoded to the correct, live verify.plotdetect.com.au, not the dead apex, not an empty string.
break_it.repro: checkout-pre-da-history.test.ts: 'falls back to the verify subdomain, never the dead bare apex, when the env var is unset'

break_it.scenario: The fix is applied inconsistently, leaving some other sibling route with the same origin-header-trust pattern undiscovered.
break_it.what_happens: A false sense that the whole payment surface is now safe when one route still isn't.
break_it.how: Grepped the entire frontend-nextjs/app/api tree for headers.get('origin') before concluding scope — only this file and the unrelated chat-honeypot route matched. Not asserted from memory of what 786fb4a7 touched; independently re-verified against the current tree.

break_it.scenario: The fix breaks the happy path for a legitimate customer on the real domain.
break_it.what_happens: Checkout would fail to redirect anywhere useful post-payment.
break_it.how: Existing happy-path tests (200 + checkout_url, success_url shape, metadata) all still pass unmodified — the fix changes only where the origin value comes from, not the URL-building logic downstream.

post_merge.db_reset: No — no database interaction in this route.
post_merge.manual_verify: Recommended but not performed here: submit a real (test-mode) pre-DA history checkout from the live app and confirm the Stripe session's success_url/cancel_url both resolve to verify.plotdetect.com.au, matching what the other checkout products already do in production.
